science.title: Hamiltonian structures, soliton orbits, and chaotic dynamics in the (2+1)-dimensional cubic-quintic Ginzburg-Landau equation
science.description: The dynamics of the $$(2+1)$$-dimensional cubic-quintic Ginzburg-Landau equation, a nonlinear optical model, are investigated. First, the equation is reduced to a traveling-wave system under specified parameter conditions, and a Hamiltonian first integral is shown to exist for the reduced system, with the traveling waves lying on its zero level. Moreover, the equilibrium points are classified; the tanh soliton is identified as a heteroclinic orbit joining three saddles, and bounded motion is confined to the two soliton loops. Then, under periodic forcing, Melnikov analysis establishes splitting of the soliton separatrix for every non-zero amplitude. Subsequently, the perturbed system orbits are classified by Lyapunov spectra, Poincaré sections, power spectra, and return maps. This analysis reveals quasi-periodic, chaotic, and unbounded behavior: a weak force turns the soliton separatrix into a thin chaotic layer from which wave profiles escape, while profiles well inside the soliton loops remain bounded and quasi-periodic. Furthermore, bounded chaotic orbits are rare and often transient; the forcing amplitude mainly controls how many profiles escape, and every bounded orbit has a Lyapunov spectrum $$(\lambda _1,0,-\lambda _1)$$. Besides, the overlap of soliton solutions is measured with a quantitative index, and a classification algorithm is applied to 20480 combinations of parameters and initial states.

science.title: The nature of the phase transition in VO2 B-phase and a quantum entanglement perspective
science.description: The well-known metal-to-insulator transition in rutile/monoclinic VO2 has been understood as a correlation-enhanced Peierls phenomenon. The lesser-known B-polymorph exhibits a similar resistivity jump, assumed to arise from an analogous transition. However, unlike rutile/monoclinic VO2, here the transition is isostructural, with dimers persisting both above and below the transition, challenging established interpretations. Here, we show that the phase transition in the B-polymorph is qualitatively different. Despite high conductivity and finite spectral weight at the chemical potential, the high-temperature phase lacks standard metallic screening and Drude peaks. Our theoretical analysis reveals that while the low-temperature insulating phase is driven by both Peierls and Mott physics, the high-temperature state is an anomalous insulator whose apparent metallicity arises from incoherent in-gap states that mimic a metal. We relate this unusual growth of incoherent states to temperature-dependent intra-dimer charge transfers. Finally, we propose a unified framework using an Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen-like quantum-entanglement measure to characterize and distinguish between different VO2 phases hosting dimers. VO2 can exist in various polymorphs. Here, the authors show that the phase transition in the B-phase of VO2 shows qualitatively different behavior from that of the well-known VO2 rutile-to-monoclinic metal-to-insulator transition.

science.title: Effect of titanium deposition duration on the surface and electrochemical performance of AISI 431 martensitic stainless steel for potential dental implant applications
science.description: This study investigated the effect of Ti deposition duration on the surface and electrochemical performance of AISI 431 martensitic stainless steel with relevance to potential dental implant applications. Ti coatings were deposited by RF magnetron sputtering for 30, 60, and 90 min, and their morphology, crystalline structure, thickness, surface roughness, apparent microhardness, and corrosion behavior in Hank’s solution were evaluated. Increasing deposition duration promoted the development of a denser granular surface morphology and modified the surface topography, while the coating thickness increased from approximately 0.96 μm for Ti-30 to approximately 8.4 μm for Ti-60 and Ti-90. XRD analysis confirmed predominantly crystalline HCP α-Ti coatings while retaining the characteristic α′-martensitic diffraction response of the AISI 431 substrate. The highest apparent microhardness was obtained for Ti-90 at 332.71 ± 3.22 HV0.01, corresponding to a 17.48% increase compared with the uncoated specimen. Potentiodynamic polarization showed that Ti-90 exhibited the lowest corrosion current density, with an Ecorr of − 0.5307 V and an icorr of 1.052 × 10⁻⁸ A cm⁻². Complementary OCP and EIS measurements further showed that Ti-90 exhibited the most favorable OCP response among the coated specimens, the highest low-frequency impedance, and the strongest capacitive behavior. Overall, the combined surface, structural, and electrochemical results identified the 90 min deposition condition as the most favorable among the investigated Ti coatings, providing a preliminary basis for further evaluation of Ti-coated AISI 431 for potential dental implant applications.

ai.title: Tec-Do and Tencent Cloud Form Strategic Partnership to Help Businesses Unlock Global Growth with AI
ai.description: SHENZHEN, China, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Tec-Do, a leading global AI marketing technology company, signed a strategic partnership agreement with Tencent Cloud on November 26. Under the agreement, the companies will deepen collaboration on large AI models for marketing, computing resources and cloud infrastructure, Model-as-a-Service (MaaS), and the Tencent WorkBuddy AI agent ecosystem. The partnership will integrate AI and cloud technologies into the workflows brands use to expand internationally, helping more businesses develop growth strategies they can scale and replicate across markets.
